title: Count page visits without losing one

blocks.text: The page's pitfall: every single call on a `ConcurrentHashMap` is atomic, but `get` followed by `put` is **two** atomic calls, not one. Two threads can both read the old count and both write the same new count, and one visit is lost. The page's Q5 shows exactly this lost update on a counter.

Write `Visits.record(ConcurrentHashMap<String, Integer> counts, String page)`. It adds one to `page`'s count, starting from 1 when the page is not in the map yet. Many threads call it at the same time on one map, and no visit may be lost.

rows: two threads each call `record(counts, "home")` at once

cases.says: Each recorded visit adds one to its page's count.
The first visit to a page not yet in the map sets its count to 1.
Two visits recorded at the same moment by two threads both count, even when both threads read the old count before either writes.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: get followed by put is two atomic calls, not one; a concurrent counter must use an atomic read-modify-write such as merge or compute, or updates are lost.
